# dsh-redline
English · Português (Brasil) · 简体中文
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-redline) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-redline) [](LICEN
SE) [](https://github.com/klaus-2/dsh-redline/releases) [](https://github.com/klaus-2/dsh-redline/di
ps://github.com/klaus-2/dsh-redline/releases) [](https://github.com/klaus-2/dsh-redline/discussions)
**Point at any element on the page. Your agent fixes the code.**
`dsh-redline` is a DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts visual review inside the harness browser: selec
t an element, leave a comment, adjust styles live, and confirm — the annotations travel to your agen
t as structured context attached to your next message, with a cropped screenshot of exactly the regi
d context attached to your next message, with a cropped screenshot of exactly the region you marked.
`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-redline`
## Why this exists
Describing a UI problem in words loses the pointer. "The button in the middle section looks off" mak
es your agent guess. Redline keeps the feedback attached to the element: selector, role, text, your
comment, a cropped screenshot, and every style tweak you tried — delivered in one structured block t
he agent can act on.
## Product tour

1. Press **C** (comment) or **V** (adjust) in any page opened in the harness browser.
2. Click an el

ement. A popover opens anchored to it.
3. Write the comment, or open the inspector and adjust text,

colors, typography, size, spacing, borders and effects — every change previews live on the page.
4.
Confirm. The card above the composer collects your pins. Send, and the annotations reach the agent a

s a snapshot alongside your message — rendered natively in the chat.
5. Press **D** for the free ann
otation canvas: brush, lines, arrows, rectangles, ellipses, numbered step markers and text — send th
e full page to the chat with every drawing composited into the screenshot.
## What the agent receives
For each pin, one block in a single snapshot:

- `Target` — tag, role, accessible label
- `Target selector` — a CSS path back to the element
- `Tar

get text` / `Component` — content and framework hints
- `Screenshot (cropped around the target)` — a

JPEG of the marked region with surrounding context
- `Comment` — what you asked for
- `Requested vi

sual changes` — every live adjustment as `prop: before -> after`
- `Requested text change` — when yo
u edited the element's text
## Features

- Element picking with hover highlight on any page the harness browser renders
- Per-pin comments, e

ditable in place, with resolve/reopen/delete
- Live style inspector with rollback: drag-to-scrub num
bers, color pickers, presets, linked box-model and radius edits, shadow and transform composers, per

-row reset
- Cropped screenshots per pin (not the whole viewport)
- Annotations attach to the next m

essage of the session you are viewing, rendered as a native chat card
- Reconciliation: removing a p

in from the card removes it from the page overlay too
- English, Português (Brasil) and 简体中文 in the
overlay UI, chosen from the browser locale

## Use
| Key | Action |

| `C` | Comment mode — pick an element, write what should change |
| `V` | Adjust mode — pick an ele

ment, open the live style inspector |
| `Esc` | Cancel the current mode, popover or preview |
| `Ent
er` | Save the annotation from the popover |
Pins collect in the card above the composer. **Send** dispatches them with your next message; the ✕
discards them, and the page overlay updates itself.
## Security notes
The loopback server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, answers only for its own host names (so a name that res
olves to 127.0.0.1 cannot reach it) and validates the Host header, so remote origins cannot reach it
. Every private route requires an instance secret that the host keeps in the profile (`~/.dsh/profil
es/<profile>/dsh-redline/instance.secret`, mode 0600) and that never reaches the page: the overlay h
olds no secret, no header and no secret in a URL.
The page talks to the host through a limited message bridge instead. It can submit the annotations,
save the drawings, read the narrow state the overlay draws (language, delivery, pending ids, setting
s) and report a diagnostic — every other route answers `401`. The host half calls the bridge with th
e secret; the page calls it from a browser request that carries this origin, and the `Origin` header
cannot be forged by a script. That origin also carries the pages the plugin proxies, so the bridge
is an annotation channel and never a data channel.
Pages running in the harness browser can submit annotations by design — that is the plugin working a
s intended, so treat comments arriving through Redline like any other user-authored input: a comment
is the text the Redline overlay captured on the page, and the pending annotations are shown in the
card above the composer before they attach to your next message. The agent ticker (tool arguments, a
gent text) stays in the host; the page only ever sees the narrow projection above. No cookies are fo
rwarded through the proxy.
## Configure
Nothing to configure by default. The plugin starts a loopback server (`127.0.0.1:47477`, falling bac
k to the next 20 ports) that serves the overlay, the screenshot attachments and the annotation intak
to the next 20 ports) that serves the overlay, the screenshot attachments and the annotation intake.
## How it works
The client face injects the overlay into every page the harness browser renders. The overlay sends t
he annotations through the message bridge, and the loopback server stores a pending snapshot keyed b
y the session you are viewing. When you send a message, the host attaches the snapshot to the agent'
s turn as a producer-owned context message with section metadata, and the chat renders it as a colla
producer-owned context message with section metadata, and the chat renders it as a collapsible card.
